name: State paid family and medical leave program contribution rates, benefits, and eligibility
description: The mandatory paid family and medical leave programs that US states operate, with each state's current contribution rate, employer/employee split, maximum weekly benefit, wage replacement formula, leave duration, covered reasons, employer-size threshold, and program launch date. As of mid-2026, 14 states plus DC operate programs: California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, DC, Maine, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Oregon, Rhode Island, and Washington. Maryland and Virginia have enacted programs launching in 2028. Contribution rates change annually (Washington rose to 1.13% for 2026; Massachusetts remains at 0.88%). Wage replacement ranges from a flat 67% (New York) to sliding scales giving 90-100% to low-wage workers (Washington, Oregon, Colorado, Minnesota). Duration ranges from 6 weeks (California family-only) to 26 weeks (Massachusetts military family). This is a production-edge asset: maintaining current rates across 15+ annually-changing programs was prohibitive for one person and is now economic. Answers 'what is the paid family leave contribution rate in [state]', 'how much paid leave do employees get in [state]', 'does my state have paid family leave', and 'what is the maximum paid leave benefit in [state]'.
licence: State program contribution rates, benefit amounts, and eligibility rules are facts from state government program pages and policy research organisations; not copyrightable.

records.wage_replacement_formula: 90 percent of wages for workers earning up to 70 percent of the average quarterly wage; 70 percent for higher earners
records.covered_reasons: bonding, own serious health condition, family caregiving, military exigency
records.source_quote: California’s law was passed in 2002, implemented in 2004, and has been amended multiple times, including in 2022 to greatly increase wage replacement beginning in 2025. The maximum length of family leave increased from six to eight weeks on July 1, 2020. See <http://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=201920200SB83> SB 83 and <https://www.edd.ca.gov/Payroll_Taxes/What_Are_State_Payroll_Taxes.htm> tax rates and wage bases . On January 1, 2021, individuals became eligible to receive up to six weeks of military exigency leave; see <https://www.edd.ca.gov/pdf_pub_ctr/de2530.pdf> California Employment Development Department . In 2026, payroll tax contributions are 1.3 percent, a slight increase from the 1.2 percent rate charged in 2025.

records.wage_replacement_formula: 90 percent of the employee's wage up to 50 percent of SAWW plus 50 percent of the employee's wage over 50 percent of SAWW; maximum benefit is 90 percent of SAWW
records.employer_size_threshold: 1 employee (small businesses exempt from employer contribution)
records.covered_reasons: bonding, own serious health condition, family caregiving, NICU leave, military exigency, safe leave
records.source_quote: In Colorado, the statute prescribed tax rates and wage bases set at .9 percent with contributions split between workers and employers for the program’s first two years, 2024 and 2025. In 2026, the rate dropped slightly to .88 percent. The taxable wage base is the Social Security cap. Small businesses are not required to contribute to the program. Colorado’s law was expanded beginning in 2026 to include an additional 12 weeks of leave for parents with babies in a neonatal intensive care unit—the first state in the country to offer NICU leave. The law also includes both military exigency leave and “safe” leave for survivors of domestic violence, stalking, and sexual assault. See <https://famli.colorado.gov/individuals-and-families> Colorado Department of Labor and Employment .

records.wage_replacement_formula: 90 percent of employee's wage up to minimum wage x 40 plus 60 percent of employee's wage over minimum wage x 40
records.medical_leave_duration: 12 weeks plus 2 weeks for pregnancy complication
records.covered_reasons: bonding, own serious health condition, family caregiving, military exigency, safe leave
records.source_quote: In Connecticut, the wage replacement calculation is based on minimum wage. Replacement rate is 90 percent of employee’s wage up to minimum wage x 40 plus 60 percent of employee’s wage over minimum wage x 40. Maximum benefit is minimum wage x 60, $1,016.40 in 2026. See <https://ctpaidleave.org/s/employee-landing-page?language=en_US> Connecticut Paid Leave .

records.employer_share: split with employee by leave type
records.employee_share: split with employer by leave type
records.wage_replacement_formula: 80 percent of the individual's average weekly wage, up to a cap of $900 per week
records.covered_reasons: bonding, own serious health condition, family caregiving
records.source_quote: Delaware’s wage replacement rate is 80 percent of the individual’s average weekly wage, up to a cap of $900 per week in the program’s first two years (2026 and 2027), with annual adjustments thereafter. The minimum benefit is $100 a week (including full wage replacement for workers who make less than $100 per week but are otherwise eligible for the program). See <https://labor.delaware.gov/delaware-paid-leave/> Delaware Benefits Calculator .

records.wage_replacement_formula: 90 percent of the employee's wage up to 150 percent of DC's minimum wage x 40 plus 50 percent of the employee's wage over 150 percent of DC's minimum wage x 40
records.covered_reasons: bonding, own serious health condition, family caregiving, prenatal leave
records.source_quote: See DC <https://dcpaidfamilyleave.dc.gov/employers/> tax rates . DC extended the duration of paid family and medical leave to a total of 12 weeks beginning in October 2022, up from an interim increase in 2021 and the program’s initial offering of just two weeks of paid medical leave, six weeks of paid caregiving leave, and eight weeks of paid parental leave. DC also offers two weeks of prenatal leave, as of October 2021; see <https://dcpaidfamilyleave.dc.gov/workers/> DC Paid Family Leave . DC reduced employer payroll contributions from .62 percent to .26 percent in 2022 and kept premiums there for 2023 and 2024. In 2025, the Council approved a premium increase to .75 percent, and that is the same rate applied in 2026. The DC paid leave fund is available for other purposes due to a 2025 statutory change allowing excess funds to be transferred to DC’s general fund. See more <https://lims.dccouncil.gov/Legislation/B25-0787> here (section 12a, page 18).

records.employer_share: 100% for employers with 15+ workers (may seek 50% from employees); 50% for employers with fewer than 15
records.employee_share: up to 50% of premium (may be withheld by employer with 15+ workers); 50% for employers with fewer than 15
records.wage_replacement_formula: 90 percent for workers with an individual average weekly wage that is 50 percent or less of SAWW plus 66 percent of wages that are above 50 percent of SAWW
records.covered_reasons: bonding, own serious health condition, family caregiving, safe leave, military exigency
records.source_quote: Maine’s wage replacement rate is 90 percent for workers with an individual average weekly wage that is 50 percent or less of SAWW plus 66 percent of wages that are above 50 percent of SAWW. The maximum benefit is the SAWW, which is $1,198.84 in 2026. See <https://www.maine.gov/paidleave/benefitcalculator/index.shtml> Maine Benefits Estimator Tool .

records.wage_replacement_formula: 90 percent for workers with an individual average weekly wage that is 65 percent or less of SAWW plus 50 percent of wages that are above 65 percent of SAWW
records.covered_reasons: bonding, own serious health condition, family caregiving
records.source_quote: Maryland’s wage replacement rate is 90 percent for workers with an individual average weekly wage that is 65 percent or less of SAWW plus 50 percent of wages that are above 65 percent of SAWW. The maximum benefit will be $1,000 a week beginning in January 2028 annually thereafter; the minimum benefit is $50 a week. See <https://paidleave.maryland.gov/about-the-program/> Maryland FAMLI program information .

records.wage_replacement_formula: 80 percent of the employee's wage up to 50 percent of SAWW plus 50 percent of the employee's wage over 50 percent of SAWW
records.covered_reasons: bonding, own serious health condition, family caregiving, military family leave
records.source_quote: See Massachusetts <https://www.mass.gov/info-details/paid-family-and-medical-leave-employer-contribution-rates-and-calculator> tax rates and wage bases . Small businesses with fewer than 25 employees are not required to contribute to premiums. The taxable wage base cap is the Social Security cap. Note that the maximum length of leave is capped at 26 weeks per year (12 weeks of family leave, 20 weeks of medical leave, and 26 weeks to care for a wounded service member). See <https://www.mass.gov/guides/workers-guide-to-paid-family-and-medical-leave#-worker-contribution-rates-> Massachusetts Family and Medical Leave . Massachusetts’ contribution rate dropped from .68 percent in 2022 to .63 percent in 2023, but jumped to .88 percent in 2024 and has remained there in 2025 and 2026.

records.wage_replacement_formula: 90 percent up to half of SAWW; 66 percent of wages between half and full SAWW; 55 percent for wages exceeding SAWW
records.covered_reasons: bonding, own serious health condition, family caregiving, military exigency, safe leave
records.source_quote: Minnesota’s wage replacement is in three tiers: 90 percent up to half of SAWW; 66 percent of workers’ wages that fall between over half and the full SAWW; and 55 percent for wages that exceed the SAWW. The maximum benefit is the same as the SAWW, which is calculated annually and is $1,423 in 2026. See <https://pl.mn.gov/resources/calculators/estimate-your-payments> Minnesota Benefits Calculator .

records.employee_share: 0.23% on the first $171,100 in covered wages
records.covered_reasons: bonding, own serious health condition, family caregiving
records.source_quote: In New Jersey, as of July 1, 2020, claimants are paid 85 percent of their average weekly wage. In 2026, the maximum weekly benefit is $1,119 per week. See <https://www.nj.gov/labor/ea/employer-services/rate-info/> New Jersey Department of Labor . Prior to July 2020, claimants were paid two-thirds of their average weekly wage, up to a maximum of $667 per week.

records.wage_replacement_formula: 67 percent of employee's weekly wage up to 67 percent of SAWW
records.source_quote: In New York, as of 2021 after four years of scaling up, the wage replacement rate reached its full amount of 67 percent of employee’s weekly wage up to 67 percent of SAWW. The maximum benefit in 2026 is $1,228.53. See <https://paidfamilyleave.ny.gov/PFLbenefitscalculator> New York Paid Family Wage Benefit Calculator . Temporary disability insurance has different wage replacement in New York, and the maximum benefit is just $170 a week; this is the only state in which TDI and PFL programs have different payment rates. Advocates are working to update TDI in New York.

records.wage_replacement_formula: 100 percent of the employee's wage up to 65 percent of SAWW plus 50 percent of the employee's wage over 65 percent of SAWW
records.covered_reasons: bonding, own serious health condition, family caregiving, safe leave
records.source_quote: In Oregon in 2026, workers and businesses will <https://www.oregon.gov/employ/NewsAndMedia/Documents/2025-11-18_Tax_Rate_2026_Press_Release.pdf> continue to contribute a combined 1 percent of payroll, just as in 2024 and 2025. The taxable wage base cap is the Social Security cap. Oregon’s law includes “safe leave” for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and stalking. Small businesses are not required to contribute to the program.

records.wage_replacement_formula: 4.62 percent of wages paid in the highest quarter of the base period
records.covered_reasons: bonding, own serious health condition, family caregiving
records.source_quote: See Rhode Island <https://dlt.ri.gov/media/13506/download?language=en> tax rates and wage bases . Rates for 2026 are 1.1 percent, returning to 2024 levels, but—beginning in 2026—premiums are assessed on more of workers’ earnings in order to pay for higher wage replacement rates. Rhode Island allows for a maximum of 30 weeks of combined annual disability and family leave. Beginning in 2026, one week of leave is available for bone marrow donation, and 30 days is available for organ donation. See <https://dlt.ri.gov/media/20456/download?language=en> Rhode Island TCI claimant pamphlet for 2026.

records.wage_replacement_formula: 90 percent of the employee's wage up to 50 percent of SAWW plus 50 percent of employee's wage over 50 percent of SAWW
records.covered_reasons: bonding, own serious health condition, family caregiving, military exigency, pregnancy loss
records.source_quote: Paid Family and Medical Leave gives Washington employees a way to take paid time off to care for themselves or a family member. You don’t have to worry about managing your employees’ claims or figuring out if they are eligible. Employees apply for Paid Leave directly with Employment Security Department. Benefits do not increase your premium. As an employer, you are not penalized for any employees, current or previous, taking their Paid Leave benefits. Your premium rate will not increase when your employees use Paid Leave benefits. Premiums, collected from employees and employers through quarterly reporting , fund the Paid Leave program. Premium rates are adjusted each year in January for wages paid in the calendar year.
